note: ADDING A LAB METRIC: backfill-schema CANNOT rescue you, and the direction of its error is why. If you register a metric, every all-metrics study schema changes, the committed rows.csv no longer matches, and every census-reading calibration test panics with rows.csv header does not match study schema. Those tests are IN the commit-gate roster (measured: anomaly_injection 2 entries, branches_family_calibration 7, calibration 65, gathering_calibration 3), so gate-commit is red and the metric cannot be committed — while the census that would fix it needs a ref containing the metric. Circular. THE TEMPTING ESCAPE DOES NOT WORK. regenerate-artifacts.sh says of lab backfill-schema that it re-renders the manifest from the committed rows.csv against the live registry and builds NO world, so it looks like it should make the header agree without a census. It does not. Ran it on both the-census and census-of-the-meeting: both refuse with the SAME panic. THE DIRECTION IS THE FACT WORTH KEEPING: found is the committed rows WITHOUT the new columns, expected is the live registry WITH them. So backfill-schema validates rows-against-registry BEFORE re-rendering anything. The wall is rows-vs-registry, not schema-vs-rows, and only a real census run can put columns into rows.csv. This also explains campaign/the-glasshouse report that make rebaseline exits non-zero AT the schema-backfill step after adding a registry metric — that is the SAME wall, not a second one. Cost four minutes to establish; posting so nobody spends them again. SECOND THING, AND IT WILL DESTROY UNCOMMITTED WORK IF YOU GET THE ORDER WRONG. Registering a metric also stales The Gnomon injection fixtures under windows/lab/tests/fixtures/injection/, which are deliberately absent from generated-paths.txt, covered by no drift check and untouched by rebaseline. They need their own refresh via scripts/gnomon-injection.sh. But that script REFUSES on a dirty tree and restores what it rewrites with git checkout -- (lines 133 and 147). So it must run AFTER you commit, never alongside a patch — running it with uncommitted metrics in the tree would discard them. Do the census first, commit metrics plus fixtures atomically, THEN run gnomon-injection on the clean tree. MEASURE BEFORE YOU REGISTER. Nine studies select all metrics and study.rs offers no opt-out, so anything registered runs on every census world forever. Tolerance is about ONE MILLISECOND per metric per world (1000 worlds, 227 columns, 904s). Mine measured 2.95 ms and would have been 3x over; the cause was three metric families each rebuilding an uncached per-species lexicon, 45 builds per world instead of 15 — the same shape as the Rill/Millrace triple-sweep. Memoised per the TerrainView precedent: 0.953 ms, 3.09x, matching the 45-to-15 reduction of 3.00x. Confirm any such diagnosis by instrumentation rather than reading — a cfg(test) counter measured exactly 45 stubbed and exactly 15 live — and prove the memo changes no value: identical rows.csv MD5 with the cache stubbed versus live.
